first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 EPU about $0.82-0.85 and revenue about $586-590M. Benzinga consensus $0.82 / $590.0M (27 Aug snapshot; Sidoti $0.82, Noble $0.85), Earnings Whispers $0.84 / $588.8M, Stockalarm revenue average $586M (range $559-613M). Sources: https://es.benzinga.com/quote/ARLP/earnings-forecasts, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/ARLP, https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/ARLP/analysts. The sources agree within 3 cents, so the bar is treated as sourced. The company's FY2026 guide (coal 33.75-35.25 Mt, $54-56/t, cost $37-39/t) is in the 2026-07-27 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001086600/000110465926086855/arlp-20260727xex99d1.htm. Whether the two to three covering analysts model the bitcoin fair-value line is not known.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest about 1.6M units at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 6.3 days to cover, against 128.66M units outstanding (about 1.2%), within a 2026 range of 1.3-1.7M (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/arlp/short-interest/). Borrow fee 0.4% in a July snapshot. Not a crowded short. The baseline's skew_25d is null. Put/call open interest is 0.21 on only 2,000 contracts total, and the ATM spread is 60% of mid, so the 5.97% event-implied move is indicative only. Run-up is +3.86% over 20 days and +1.44% over 5 days; the stock is 9.9% below its 52-week high.

evidence.text: ARLP held 646 bitcoins worth $37.9M at 30 June 2026 (about $58.7k each) and booked a $6.3M Q2 fair-value loss. Bitcoin closed Q3 up 42.71% at about $83.7k, which implies a Q3 mark-to-market gain of roughly $15-16M if the holding was unchanged. That is a swing of about +$22M (about +$0.17 per unit on 128.66M units) against Q2, on a bar of $0.82-0.85 that rose from $0.78 before the Q2 print. The gain is excluded from adjusted EBITDA and DCF, so it lifts headline EPU only.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 2026 bitcoin fell about 22% (an $11.7M loss) and the stock still rose 2.21% on the print. In Q2 2026, a $6.3M loss, it rose 3.72%. In Q3 2025 a $3.7M gain came with +4.12%. The line has never visibly driven the reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: The bar's step from $0.61 to $0.82-0.85 is explained by the guided H2 coal and royalty recovery alone (see the next finding). If the two or three covering analysts had added a ~$0.12-0.17 bitcoin gain, the bar would sit nearer $0.95. With bitcoin up 43%, a stock pricing the gain should have run up more than 3.9% over 20 days. The line sits below operating income and has no path to the guide or the distribution, which is why it is sized as a fraction of the same money earned as operating profit.
evidence.independence: Independent price series: Forklog/CoinGlass Q3 close of +42.71% at about $83.7k (https://forklog.com/en/?p=104576) and COINOTAG via edgeX, 2026-10-01 (https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/bitcoin-q3-2026-best-quarter-since-2017). Holding count and value come from the company's Q2 release; the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1086600/000110465926092001/arlp-20260630x10q.htm) reports no post-quarter sale.

evidence.text: The 27 July release says Hamilton is back on longwall production with no further longwall moves until 2027, and 2026 sales are 'essentially fully committed at the midpoint'. H1 sold 16.42 Mt at a segment cost of about $40/t (Q1 $41.42, Q2 $38.68). The guidance midpoint (34.5 Mt, $37-39/t) therefore implies about 9.0 Mt a quarter in H2 at roughly $36-37/t, against Q2's 8.56 Mt and $38.68. This is the improvement the market was told to expect.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume and cost recoveries signalled the quarter before were bought modestly: Q2 2026 delivered the signalled sequential volume rise (8.56 vs 7.86 Mt) and the stock rose 3.72%. In October 2025, when Appalachian setbacks cut guidance, the print still rose 4.12%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the Q3 bar rose from $0.78 (24 July) to $0.82 (27 August) after the release, which is the market writing this in. Only the gap between a delivered H2 run-rate and a merely guided one is unpriced, which is why the size is near zero.
evidence.independence: Same document as the guidance. Consensus migration is from Benzinga (https://es.benzinga.com/quote/ARLP/earnings-forecasts).

evidence.text: EIA weekly estimates reported by Argus on 10 September 2026 put Illinois Basin output (IL, IN, western KY, where ARLP is a major producer) down 6.2% year on year at about 11.6M st for Q3 to date. US output was down 4.1% over the 10 weeks to 5 September, and EIA forecasts Q3 US production of 130.9M st against 135.9M st in Q3 2025. The bar implies ARLP's Q3 coal volume rising to about 9 Mt, roughly flat to up on Q3 2025's 8.7 Mt.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume shortfalls have been looked through: the Q3 2025 print came with a cut to 2025 sales guidance and the stock rose 4.12%. The Q2 2025 volume and price softness print fell 1.72%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Industry weekly production data are not read through to ARLP by its two or three covering analysts, whose bar moved up after July. Had the market read it, the Q3 revenue bar ($586-590M) would sit nearer the Q2 run-rate ($551.6M) rather than up about 7%. The size is small because it is a proxy, and the company's own primary-document statement (2026 essentially fully committed at the midpoint, Hamilton back on longwall) cuts against transmission to ARLP specifically.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. A partial weekly data point is consistent: SXCoal citing EIA had Illinois state output down 8.5% y/y in the week to 29 August (https://en.sxcoal.com/news/detail/2095681120576409602). The company's own contracted book points the other way.

evidence.text: S&P Global (15 October 2026) says US coal stockpiles stayed high and constrained domestic price gains in September, and expects elevated 2026 stockpiles to limit demand into 2027. That bears on the 2027 committed and priced tonnage the Q3 release normally updates (29.4 Mt for 2027 at Q2) and on any preliminary 2027 commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 prints carry the first read on next year's book. The Q3 2025 print (2025 guidance cut, 2026 contracting update) rose 4.12%. No print in the baseline fell more than 3.83% (Q1 2025, February 2025).
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock is 9.9% below its 52-week high but up 3.9% over 20 days, which is not the pattern of a market pricing a weaker 2027 book. If 2027 risk were priced, the 2027 committed-tonnage line would not be expected to grow. The size is small because this is a market-level read (snippet only, page 403 to fetch) that the company has not confirmed.
evidence.independence: The June/July S&P piece 'Slack demand, surging inventory pressurize US coal prices' points the same way (https://hellenicshippingnews.com/slack-demand-surging-inventory-pressurize-us-coal-prices). The next finding is partly offsetting and comes from the same S&P October document.

evidence.text: Illinois Basin 11,500 mid-sulfur spot rose $0.75 to $54.75/st in September 2026 (S&P Global), above ARLP's Illinois Basin realised $51.87/t in Q2 and its $50-52 guide. EIA describes June-August 2026 as exceptionally hot, with Henry Hub averaging $2.93. This supports pricing on 2027 tons still to be contracted and any spot sales.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing commentary on next year's book has accompanied up-moves in 4 of the last 5 prints (2.21% to 4.12%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Benchmark-to-company transmission is slow, because ARLP's 2026 book is fixed and 2027 pricing is disclosed only on calls. If the market had priced a firmer IB spot, the 2027 price would already be talked up in previews, and no Q3 2026 preview was found. The size is small for the same proxy reason.
evidence.independence: Hot summer and low gas: EIA analysis of 25 September 2026 cited via https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68204. The spot figure shares a document with the stockpile finding above. The two can both be true: spot is up modestly while stockpiles stay high.

evidence.text: Oil and gas royalty pricing fell in Q3: WTI averaged about $94-95 in Q2 2026 (ARLP realised $49.43/BOE) but about $79 from 1 July to 8 August per the Dallas Fed. The AllDale III/IV acquisition, closed 1 July, adds about 48,500 net royalty acres, raised FY volume guidance, and is consolidated from Q3 with Craft-related entities holding $100M of AllDale III limited partner interests, which raises noncontrolling interest.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: A record royalty segment (Q2 2026, $46.3M revenue, +30.5% y/y) came with +3.72%. The segment is about 8% of revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: The oil price is public, and volume is guided, so this is mostly priced. What may not be modelled is the accounting: consolidating AllDale III inflates royalty revenue but shifts part of it to noncontrolling interest. Net of the coal segment (about 85% of revenue) this is a small line.
evidence.independence: The consolidation language is in the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1086600/000110465926092001/arlp-20260630x10q.htm). Q2 WTI is also in the Montana tax table (https://revenue.mt.gov/taxes/natural-resource-taxes/crude-oil-prices/).

evidence.text: Q2 distribution coverage was 1.39x ($108.2M DCF), up 39% sequentially. Q3 coverage should rise further on higher H2 cash flow, but management's stated priorities after the $206M AllDale purchase (funded partly by a new $150M term loan) are leverage reduction and disciplined acquisitions, so the $0.60 quarterly distribution is most likely held. A cut is very unlikely; a raise would be an unguided upside tail.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The distribution has been $0.60 since the Q1 2025 cut from $0.70. That February 2025 print was the worst reaction in the baseline (-3.83%). The four flat-distribution prints since then were +0.63, -1.72, +4.12 and +3.65.
evidence.why_not_priced: At a $2.40 annualised yield of about 9.2% on $26.12, the market prices a held distribution. A raise is not in any preview found and would show up as a lower yield. The size is small because management signalled deleveraging first.
evidence.independence: Same document. The Quartr Q2 summary repeats the leverage-reduction focus and describes no distribution change (https://quartr.com/events/alliance-resource-partners-lp-arlp-q2-2026_ozmz0e5W).

evidence.text: Insider flow into the print is negligible. Officer Mark A. Watson filed a Form 144 on 15 September 2026 to sell 6,606 units (about $173k) acquired as equity compensation, and director Ronna McDaniel's only Form 4 (18 August) is a 69.74-unit purchase at $25.81, a reinvestment-sized amount. No Form 4 from Craft was found in 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: insider flow has not been a line this name trades on.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public and immaterial. It is filed for completeness because the absence of an insider cluster ahead of the print is itself information.
evidence.independence: Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1086600/000204731926000002/xslF345X06/form4-08202026_010815.xml

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 Core FFO/share consensus $0.79 from two sources: Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/DEA via search snippet; the same site put Q2 at $0.78 vs $0.79, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/DEA) and Benzinga's Q3'26E of $0.79 (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/DEA/earnings-forecasts, search snippet; page 403 on fetch). The FY2026 guide is $3.07-$3.13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001622194/000162219426000024/dea-ex99_1.htm). With H1 at $1.55, the midpoint implies about $0.775 a quarter for H2, so $0.79 sits inside the guide's upper half. FY2026 consensus is $3.09-3.10 (Seeking Alpha / Earnings Whispers). FY2027 consensus: UNSOURCED (only a proprietary model figure was found), so the 2027-guide findings are capped small.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 2,138,684 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 4.52% of shares outstanding (higher as a share of float), 3.78 days to cover. It has risen at four straight settlements from 1.90M on 2026-08-14 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dea/short-interest). That is a slow build, not a crowded short. No usable options chain: ATM legs are not two-sided, skew is null, put/call OI is 0.73 on only 170 contracts. Sell-side is Hold-leaning: Benzinga shows 1 Buy, 4 Hold and 1 Sell; RBC is Underperform with a $24 target (2026-08-24) and Truist is Hold with a $26 target (2026-08-27). Earnings Whispers puts the post-Q2 drift at -9.1%, and the stock is 12% off its 52-week high, though up 3.1% over 5 days.

evidence.text: The FAA Great Lakes Regional Office is committed to GSA and OMB to vacate 2300 E. Devon Ave, Des Plaines by October 2026; its occupancy agreement expires 2026-10-20 and it moves to a 108,094 RSF space in Rosemont. It occupies about 186k RSF; the last GSA-published total annual cost was $5.1M (2000 lease). The Q3 release is the first document to state the post-October status, and the first 2027 guide carries a full year of that vacancy, worth an estimated $0.06-0.09/share of NOI, about 2-3% of the ~$3.10 Core FFO base, unless it is re-let or the FAA holds over.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the first-year-guide line. On 2025-10-27, the day the 2026 guide ($3.05-3.12, midpoint below the $3.11 consensus) came out, the stock fell 4.0%. On 2026-08-03 the FY guide went up $0.01 at the midpoint despite a $0.01 quarterly miss, and the stock rose 3.82%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The move-out is public and management told analysts on the Q2 call 'I would not add additional revenue in your model', so consensus 2026 likely excludes FAA rent after October. What is not public is the 2027 cost: the vacancy, carry costs and any re-let or disposal plan for a Class B suburban Chicago building, plus whether the FAA holds over (management said it was 'optimistic that they may stay a little bit longer' and promised an update). If that cost were priced, a 2027 consensus visibly below the 2-3% growth target would exist; none could be found. The upside tail (a holdover or extension) is in the range.
evidence.independence: Management's own Q2 2026 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-easterly-government-properties-inc-stock/) confirms the October end and the instruction not to model more revenue. CoStar/WGN report the Rosemont lease at 42% smaller (https://www.costar.com/article/1419709252/faa-signs-largest-office-lease-this-year-in-chicago-suburbs). The RSF and rent come from the GSA FY2020 prospectus PIL-01-OH20 (https://gsa.gov/system/files/FY2020%20IL%20Chicago%20O%27Hare%20Area%20Department%20of%20Transportation%20Federal%20Aviation%20Administration.pdf); the current rent may differ.

evidence.text: The $127.5M Loma Linda mortgage at 3.6% matures in summer 2027, and management's primary plan is an investment-grade unsecured issuance with the revolver as a bridge. At roughly 5.5% that adds about $2.4M a year of interest, about $0.025/share in 2027 for half a year. The first 2027 guide will have to absorb it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same first-guide line as above (Oct 2025 -4.0%). No prior refinancing-driven reaction found.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was disclosed on the call, but it only reaches a published number when 2027 guidance appears. Analysts on a Hold-heavy name may already model it, which is why it is sized small. If it were fully in the 2027 consensus, the guide midpoint would come in at or above consensus despite it.
evidence.independence: Shares the call transcript with the FAA finding and the acquisition-threshold finding, but rests on a different fact (debt maturity versus tenant). The 10-Q debt schedule shows $149.3M of mortgage debt at 2026-06-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001622194/000162219426000024/dea-ex99_1.htm).

evidence.text: On the Q2 call the CEO said acquisitions become possible at $24.50-25.50, 'a couple hundred million' at $26-27 and 'very material' volume at $28-30. Spot is $22.505, below every tier, so the 2027 guide is likely to assume little external growth. He named JV capital with a sovereign wealth fund partner as the alternative if the stock does not improve by late 2026 or early 2027.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 guide assumed only $50M of acquisitions, and that guide day was -4.0%. No precedent was found for a JV announcement.
evidence.why_not_priced: The share price is public and the thresholds were said aloud, but the guide's acquisition assumption is not out yet. A JV announcement with the release would be the upside tail, which is why the high end is positive.
evidence.independence: Same transcript as the two findings above. The stock is down 9.1% since the print, per Earnings Whispers PEAD (search snippet, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/DEA).

evidence.text: Supports for the 2027 guide: procurement covers expirations 'through much of 2027', with mid-to-high-teens net effective rent growth expected. The FDLE Fort Myers lab (about 64k RSF, 25-year non-cancelable lease with the AAA State of Florida) is due to deliver in H2 2026 and starts rent. Lump-sum development reimbursements also delever without new equity.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide raise on 2026-08-03 coincided with a +3.82% day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The delivery timing and rent-growth assumptions only become a number when the 2027 guide is published. The post-Q2 drift of -9.1% and Hold ratings suggest the market is not paying for them. If it were, the stock would sit near its 52-week high rather than 12% below it.
evidence.independence: The Q2 2026 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-easterly-government-properties-inc-stock/) repeats delivery 'later this year' and the rent-growth expectation. This offsets the FAA finding on the same guidance line; the two are netted by being filed separately with opposite signs.

evidence.text: The Q3 Core FFO bar of $0.79 (two agreeing sources) sits above the ~$0.775/quarter H2 run-rate implied by the $3.07-3.13 guide midpoint and above Q2's $0.78. Q2 ATM issuance (796,943 shares) dilutes, no Q3 acquisition 8-K was filed, and the FDLE lab has not delivered. A $0.78 print, a 1c miss, is somewhat more likely than a beat.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 missed by $0.01 ($0.78 vs $0.79) and the stock still rose 3.82% on the guide raise. Q3 2025 was in line at $0.76 and the stock fell 4.0% on the guide. The quarterly line has not driven this stock; the guide has.
evidence.why_not_priced: It lands inside what the company guided, so it is mostly a told-to-expect item and is sized near zero. If the market expected a miss, the bar would be $0.78.
evidence.independence: EDGAR filing list shows no 8-K after 2026-08-05 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001622194&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). That is consistent with no Q3 acquisitions.

evidence.text: On 2026-08-04/05 DEA refreshed its $300M ATM, with $215M left and new contingent and non-contingent forward-sale structures across eight counterparties. The Q3 release will show how much equity was sold in Q3 at ~$22-24, below the price management called attractive.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on ATM disclosure. Q2's $18.8M ATM raise at $23.86 coincided with a +3.82% day.
evidence.why_not_priced: What the money buys: development investment of $50-100M and deleveraging, both corroborated by three projects under construction. Management said deliveries reach target leverage 'without a need to raise additional equity'. So the sign is near zero, with a small negative if Q3 issuance was large at sub-$23 prices. The amount sold is unknown until the release or 10-Q.
evidence.independence: The Q2 release reports the ATM sales (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001622194/000162219426000024/dea-ex99_1.htm).

evidence.text: The Loma Linda mortgage refinancing itself, and any investment-grade unsecured issuance, executes in summer 2027. Only its inclusion in the 2027 guide is inside the window, and that is filed above.
Earnings Whispers revenue consensus of $94.52M for Q3 against Q2's $92.4M with no Q3 acquisitions, a possible revenue miss

FDLE lab delivery or completion announcement: none found

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS is the line this name trades on: Q2 2026 beat by $0.05-0.06 (revenue missed) +3.67%; Q1 2026 record +3.12%; Q4 2025 record (+24% NI) +4.20%; Q3 2025 missed by ~1c -5.14% (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/lakeland-financial-eports-q3-eps-1-03-consensus-1-04-thefly). 5 of 7 baseline reactions up.

evidence.text: The Q3 GAAP print very likely includes a large swap mark-to-market gain. River City's undesignated interest-rate swaps (about 17% of its swap book at 30 Jun 2026) hedge medium-term fixed-rate loans and gain when rates rise. Its own releases record +$4.3m in Q1-24 on rising rates, -$6.4m in Q1-25 (5y -42bp), +$1.73m in Q1-26 (5y +19bp) and +$3.18m in Q2-26 (5y +27bp), about $0.09-0.15m per bp. The 5-year Treasury rose 90bp in Q3-26 (4.19% on 30 Jun to 5.09% on 30 Sep) and the 2-year rose 74bp. That implies a Q3 pre-tax MTM gain of about $6-12m, or +$0.30-0.60 a share on ~14.0m shares after ~30% tax. Consensus is about $1.26 (Q2 core excluding MTM ~ $1.21), so GAAP EPS could print around $1.55-1.85, and revenue around $45-50m against the $38-39m revenue consensus. Caveats folded into the size: management states it does not treat MTM as economic, the bank may have designated more swaps during Q3 (undesignated share went 15% to 17% in Q2), and the 5y had fallen back to 4.78% by 22 Oct, so a Q4-to-date reversal of roughly a third is visible to anyone who asks on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No usable reaction history. RCBC listed on Nasdaq on 2026-08-06 and this is its first print as a listed company; earlier prints were OTC and the baseline has no EDGAR history (bank-level FDIC filer). The company itself has flagged MTM as non-economic since at least Q1-24, so holders who knew the name OTC are used to looking through it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.22-1.27 sits at or below Q2's GAAP $1.37 and at Q2's core excluding MTM, so the estimates carry no material MTM gain. The revenue consensus ($38-39m) is below Q2's $40.5m GAAP revenue, which included a $3.2m MTM gain. If the market had priced a GAAP blowout, the estimate range would sit near $1.6-1.8. The stock's +8% 20-day run may partly reflect rates-sensitive bank buying, but it carries no label. What stays unpriced is the headline 'beat' that screeners and aggregators will print. Whether holders pay for it is the open question, so the size is a fraction of the same dollars as core profit.
